practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Easier root-cause identification. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if exactly one Act operation/one assertion block. DECISION RULES: Count distinct Act operations; if >1 => non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the method performs multiple operations (insereAresta, obterAgm, imprime) in sequence, indicating multiple acts rather than a single focused Arrange-Act-Assert.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests; use setup/teardown. RATIONALE: Enables any-order execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if use local variables or proper Before/After. DECISION RULES: If only local variables used, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test uses only local variables and does not rely on shared mutable state or inter-test dependencies.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should check both happy and error paths. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if there are at least two tests covering happy and error cases or explicit exception assertions. DECISION RULES: If class only tests happy path with no exception tests, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because only a single test exists and it executes a normal flow without any exception or invalid-input checks, and no assertThrows/@Test(expected) usage.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary values. RATIONALE: Catches off-by-one and range errors. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if test data includes empty/zero/negative/max values or names indicate boundary intent. DECISION RULES: If all data are typical and no explicit boundary cases present, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test uses arbitrary large integers but does not exercise or document boundary conditions (e.g., zero, -1, Integer.MAX_VALUE) or edge-case indices.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if helper methods or constants exist or tests are very short and non-repetitive. DECISION RULES: If tests are very short (<10 lines) and don't repeat code, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the method is short and self-contained with no duplicated blocks across multiple methods (only one method present).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and low complexity. RATIONALE: Easier to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if method is short (<20 lines) and has no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: If method <15 lines and linear, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test is short (5 lines in body) and contains no loops or conditionals.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple properties to catch subtle faults. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may miss bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if multiple properties of results are checked (>=2). DECISION RULES: If only 0-1 superficial assertions, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test contains no assertions at all, so it does not verify properties of results thoroughly.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or commented-out tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests hide defects. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if there are no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests. DECISION RULES: Search for @Ignore/@Disabled or commented @Test; if none, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant — the test is active (annotated with @Test) and contains no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be linked to requirements. RATIONALE: Improves tracking. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if annotations or Javadoc reference requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: If class-level Javadoc includes 'REQ-' or similar, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the class-level Javadoc explicitly contains 'Traceability: REQ-AGM-001', providing traceability.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be explicit. RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements matter. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if explicit performance annotations (e.g., @Test(timeout=...)) present. DECISION RULES: Mark as compliant only if explicit performance tests seen. VERDICT: compliant because the test method uses @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit timing constraint indicating a performance-related assertion.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Names make tests self-documenting. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if names follow method_scenario_expected pattern. DECISION RULES: Generic names like 'test1' are non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the method name 'test1' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected behavior.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid verbose autogenerated tests. RATIONALE: Generated tests are hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: non-compliant if signs of auto-generation (auto comments, test0/test1 names) present. DECISION RULES: If auto-generated naming/patterns appear, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the class uses EvoSuite runner/parameters, EvoAssertions imports, and a generic method name 'test1' — clear signs of test generation rather than hand-crafted minimal tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD naming). RATIONALE: TDD/BDD yields better coverage. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming present. DECISION RULES: If tests are minimal and lack Given-When-Then or edge/error coverage, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the single test lacks Given-When-Then structure in the method body and does not show evidence of thoughtful prioritization or multiple scenario coverage.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should verify behavior through public APIs, not internals. RATIONALE: Reduces brittleness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if tests call public methods and do not use reflection. DECISION RULES: If no reflection/internal access is used, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test only constructs objects and calls public methods (Grafo, insereAresta, AgmPrim, obterAgm, imprime) and does not use reflection or access private/internal state.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include messages. RATIONALE: Improves failure diagnostics. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if assertions include descriptive messages or specific assertEquals/assertThat usage. DECISION RULES: If no assertions or only generic assertTrue used, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test contains no assertions at all, so it fails to validate outcomes; improved assertions with messages are necessary.

PRINCIPLE: Use minimal, value-adding comments. RATIONALE: Comments should explain 'why'. EVALUATION CRITERIA: non-compliant if commented-out code or excessive comments present. DECISION RULES: If no commented-out code and comments are minimal, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because there is a concise class-level Javadoc and no commented-out code or excessive inline comments in the test method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be deterministic (no random/time/external dependencies). RATIONALE: Avoids flaky tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if no Random/System.currentTimeMillis/Thread.sleep or external dependencies used. DECISION RULES: If none of those are present in the method, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the method contains no randomness, time-based calls, sleeps, or external network/database interactions (despite EvoSuite runner, the method itself is deterministic).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not produce persistent side effects or shared-state changes. RATIONALE: Prevents inter-test interference. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if local variables only and no persistent resources are modified without cleanup. DECISION RULES: If only local state is modified and no external resources are used, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test modifies only local Grafo instance in-memory and does not create files, DB records, or static modifications requiring cleanup.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories (e.g., @Tag/@Category) to classify tests. RATIONALE: Facilitates selective execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if @Tag/@Category or @Category at class/method level present. DECISION RULES: If @Category or similar annotations exist, mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization.
